title: Ten low-noise modes retained 69 to 72 percent of fitted noise reduction between two adult worm site-release models
abstract: We fitted ten low-noise modes to each of two adult worm synaptic site maps and applied them to the other map. Under shared site release with equal positive contact effects and independent sites, mean variance ratios were 0.6366 and 0.6150 relative to independent contact release. The modes retained 69.0 and 72.2 percent of their fitted noise reduction. Both results were below all 1,999 sampled label controls within joint input-count quartile bins. The adjusted Monte Carlo p value was 0.001 in each direction. Five-mode and twenty-mode checks and raw donor weights also gave ratios below one. These are conditional anatomical model results. Only two adults were used. Unknown release dependence, target gains, signs, signal tuning and omitted cells limit the result. Low noise alone does not show useful coding. Code, aggregate results, input hashes, external retrieval instructions and a figure support reproduction. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Mean model variance in ten donor-fitted modes after transfer. The independent-contact reference is one. Pair-specific panels differ outside the adult comparison. No animal population intervals are shown.

citations.reason: Reuses the attributed 162-cell panel. Extends within-map variance bounds to subspace transfer. No site tables or matrices reused.
Prior adult transfer test fixed signal-response constraints. This test transfers a low-noise subspace without a signal constraint.
Prior pooled-rank and signal-cancellation result limits interpretation of low-noise modes.
